item.title: The FDA wants to pull its approval of a drug. It’s not so easy.
item.author: Sara Talpos, Undark Magazine
item.content:encoded: In May 2021, the US Food and Drug Administration released a lengthy briefing document on an experimental medication for a rare autoimmune form of vasculitis that often damages the kidneys and lungs. The agency was on the fence about whether to approve the treatment, and it wanted an independent advisory committee to weigh in. Among the questions at hand: Was the drug meaningfully better than existing therapies?Participants in the study, which had been conducted by the California biotechnology company ChemoCentryx, did appear to have slightly higher rates of symptom remission after one year. But according to the FDA, it was hard to interpret the results because the study’s design had been less than optimal. Some advisory committee members expressed a similar view. The effect of the drug, said one, “is just not well verified by this study.”At the same time, many patients, and some physicians, saw in the data a potentially helpful medication, one that might lessen patients’ reliance on steroids, which are highly effective but often cause severe side effects.

item.title: Winners and losers from MotoGP's Sepang sprint
item.author: Eden Hannigan
item.content:encoded: Sepang produced another chaotic MotoGP sprint, as Pedro Acosta walked away with the race victory and Marc Marquez established an ever-increasing grip on the riders’ title. After the 10-lap sprint in near-mixed conditions, here are our winners and losers. Winner: Pedro Acosta (1st)Out of Acosta's three various-distance race wins in MotoGP so far, this one may well be the nicest - though he admitted it owed a lot to him having no championship implications to worry about unlike Marquez and Marco Bezzecchi.Considering he isn't really convinced about his strengths in this kind of mixed weather, this was an important win, too, and certainly not something that would dissuade you if you have him pegged as a 2027 title favourite.Winner: Marc Marquez (2nd)Marquez marches on, muffling the heartbeats of the already on-life-support title battle. This was a slightly precarious race, though not quite as precarious as it could've been. It was just controllable enough for Marquez to control it exactly to his liking - as his gameplan was to stay ahead of Bezzecchi but also to not lead, to not be the pathfinder having to figure out the wet patches.It worked out well, and while he should have been beaten by his brother today, he wasn't, meaning that it's now been 12 races (across GPs and sprints) since Marquez last wasn't the top Ducati in the classification.Loser: Alex Marquez (DNF)It’s not too far-fetched to say the younger Marquez was a pre-weekend contender for a potential 37-point haul, and he looked well on-course when he took pole position and built up a healthy lead three laps into the sprint.His error that might’ve come from “too much confidence” after his first pole since the 2025 Catalan GP or being “too optimistic” going into Turn 14 threw away a very likely 12 points - and, already injured, it's fortunate he's come away unscathed from what was a fairly high-speed off.“It’s something tomorrow that we need to control a bit more,” was Marquez’s assessment of that specific corner. At least he’s lucky to have a second go at it, and he normally learns his lessons from Saturday to Sunday. Loser: Jack Miller (DNF) and Pramac YamahaEverybody involved is more than a little lucky here that the rain didn't unfold like Miller thought it might in pitting at the end of the second lap.Running 18th, with no hope of points, and aware that a deluge was coming at some point, Miller hoped to pre-empt it by pitting - and arrived to a spare bike that hadn't been swapped to wets."I had a chat with Giacomo [Guidotti, crew chief] before the race, I said 'have the bike ready'," Miller explained afterwards. "In my mind that was, like, have the bike ready immediately. In his mind that was, like, four-five laps. So, miscommunication and unfortunately today we look like w***ers."Luckily for Pramac, Miller's gamble would have never worked with the way the rain played out. But imagine if a potential win had been thrown away in this way.So close to a maiden sprint victory but coming up short due to his lack of wet-weather confidence, it was still an impressive display of (mostly) contained aggression from Ogura. Getting a good launch from the second row of the grid, Ogura went all-out against Marquez in the opening corners of the sprint, and eventually got the better of the Ducati rider throughout the first phase of the race.It didn’t last, thanks to the mixed conditions the Trackhouse Aprilia rider hates, and he crossed the line in fourth, which was still a mega effort and also much better than Ogura himself had anticipated.“Last in the group, so there’s no reason to be happy,” was his ever self-critical description.Winner: Brad Binder (7th)Yes, Binder's seventh place pales in comparison with what Acosta managed eight seconds up the road - but you take the wins where you can get them, and Binder badly needed one this weekend.He has looked totally out of sorts over one lap here, worse than usual, but basically undid all the damage from a poor qualifying into Turn 1.There was a bit of back-and-forth combat from there, and some wet-weather improvisation, so it's not a huge surprise Binder came off well - beating Enea Bastianini and only just coming up short of picking off Pecco Bagnaia.Winner: Diogo Moreira (8th)Moreira made his life a bit harder than it needed to be with a mistake early on in the race - but was afforded the opportunity to make up for it by the weather.He seemed to thrive in the cagey late-race conditions relative to those around him, working his way past the battling duo of Johann Zarco and Enea Bastianini for a rock-solid eighth place.In the context of just this race, the performance of the two remaining Aprilias was actually pretty good considering Sepang has long been one of its nemesis circuits for the RS-GP. However, in the broader scheme of 2026, where it just lost its most valuable asset in Jorge Martin and is praying for a miracle with Bezzecchi, it’s a circuit where it cannot afford to be outscored by Marquez. But that’s exactly what happened on Saturday, despite the best efforts of Ogura to disrupt the Ducati rider’s momentum. In a race that threatened chaos, it could have been one to upset Marquez, and it just didn't.Similarly, Bezzecchi could have thrown caution to the wind and just gone for it, knowing he has no pressure and no real championship chance. He didn’t, only passing Ogura - who steadfastly denied Aprilia orders hinted at by Marquez.Ogura's denial rings true, but nobody would really begrudge Aprilia if it did want to try to keep its riders' title aspirations alive through team orders. As it stands, even team orders would be nowhere near enough.

item.title: Trump beware: US voters are concerned about government corruption
item.author: Eduardo Porter
item.content:encoded: Alleged self-dealing by the president and his allies doesn’t look so good as corruption emerges as a key issue for midterm votersVoters under 50 probably won’t remember the “welfare queen”. But she once embodied Republicans’ claim of the underlying reason for US societal decay: the poor are a bunch of fraudsters.Ronald Reagan introduced Linda Taylor to US voters at a rally during the Republican presidential primary season in 1976. A resident of Chicago’s South Side, Taylor had been arrested for welfare fraud. “She used 80 names, 30 addresses, five phone numbers to collect food stamps, social security, veteran’s benefits for four non-existing deceased veteran husbands,” Reagan said. “Her tax-free cash income alone has been running $150,000 a year.”The Qatari government gifted him a luxury jet, potentially violating the emoluments clause of the constitution.The UAE gained access to some tightly guarded, high-end American AI chips soon after an investment firm linked to its ruling family secretly bought a $500m stake in World Liberty Financial, the crypto company funded by the families of Trump and his chum Steve Witkoff.Rich people facing criminal charges have taken to donating to Trump’s political operations and then seeking pardons or clemency. Most recently, Wanda Vázquez Garced, the former governor of Puerto Rico, and the banker who paid her bribes, Julio Herrera Velutini, were pardoned after Velutini’s family gave a $50m deal to Alina Habba, Trump’s former personal lawyer, and donated $3.5m to Trump’s Maga Inc Super Pac.The first family is also making a killing from the government. The Pentagon lent more than $600m to Vulcan Elements, a rare earths startup, just three months after Donald Jr’s venture capital firm 1789 Capital bought a stake in the outfit.Powerus, a drone maker backed by Eric and Donald Jr is selling drone interceptors to Persian Gulf allies of the US that are under attack by Iran, enriching the kids from a misbegotten war launched by the dad without consulting Congress.Continue reading...

item.title: The staggering $446m Elon Musk has spent on the US midterms – visualized

item.content:encoded: The tech mogul’s midterm donations backing Republicans have made him the largest single-cycle political donor in modern US historyElon Musk has poured so much money into US politics this midterms election cycle that his donations could fund half a dozen SpaceX rocket launches or buy thousands of Tesla Cybertrucks. At the Tesla Diner in Los Angeles, Musk could order more than 31.9m cheeseburgers with the money he has spent on the midterms.Musk, the world’s richest person, has funnelled at least $445.77m into Republican-aligned political action committees (Pacs) and groups since last year, according to US Federal Election Commission data as of 29 October. The contributions have made him the Republicans’ most prominent financial backer and the largest single-cycle political donor in modern US history.Continue reading...

item.title: Today on Pinstripe Alley – 10/31/26
item.author: Andrew Mearns
item.content:encoded: This year’s Halloween marks the 25th anniversary of one of the most famous moments in modern Yankees history. Just a little while before midnight, Tino Martinez stepped up to the plate as the Bombers’ last hope of avoiding a 3-1 World Series deficit against the Arizona Diamondbacks. It’s easy to forget now, but Byung-Hyun Kim struck out the side in a perfect eighth even before retiring two of the first three batters in the ninth. However, Paul O’Neill singled with one down, and two batters later, up came Tino.Hell of a moment! Right after midnight, Derek Jeter walked it off in the 10th.Today on the site, Michael will check in on this past week’s Arizona Fall League action from Dax Kilby and company, Jonathan will celebrate the 64th birthday of solid catcher Matt Nokes, and John will take the occasion of Halloween to remember the decisions that most haunt the Yankees in the past decade. Also, Matt will name his All-October Yankees Birthdays team.1. I’m sure we’ve asked this before, but it’s that time of year again: favorite Halloween candy?2. When candy isn’t offered: pretzels or popcorn?

item.title: Wahoo CEO talks finances, artificial intelligence and the company's 'next big opportunity'
item.author: josh.croxton@futurenet.com (Josh Croxton)
item.content:encoded: Wahoo Fitness has returned to year on year growth following its recapitalisation in 2023, CEO Gareth Joyce has revealed. Speaking exclusively to , Joyce opened up on a broad range of subjects, including why it took so long to update the Kickr Core despite growing the Kickr to its sixth iteration, why it launched a treadmill, the reasoning behind its partnership with Coros, and why 2038 is going to be a heck of a busy year. He outlined a business very much with cycling still at its centre, but explained that running taking increasing amounts of importance. And he explained that there’s a busy product roadmap ahead, with "seven or eight" launches in the pipeline for 2027 following a year spent reorganising developmentJoyce, an engineer and keen cyclist and runner who joined Wahoo in 2024, had never worked in the bike industry before and admits he wasn’t an obvious candidate for the CEO role, but that his then-recent experience talking a company through Chapter 11 bankruptcy made him perfectly qualified given Wahoo’s financial turbulence at the time. He sees his role as bringing a sense of corporate structure to a startup business. He explained that Wahoo’s foundations were built on innovation, but its scale no longer supports that model of working. "It’s no longer just a startup," he said. "We’ve got a large customer base that you have a responsibility to."Asked whether the changes following Wahoo’s recapitalisation are working, Joyce’s answer was pretty conclusive."We’ve had very strong growth coming out of that," he said. "We have a great brand, great product, very committed customer base, and there were some things we needed to fix in the business which we paid attention to early on."We’ve seen growth year over year in all of the years since the recapitalisation, and I expect this year to be the same."Naturally, he declined to provide any actual figures, so the extent of Wahoo’s profitability will have to remain unknown, but he affirmed that key "operational changes" are key to the business’s newfound momentum. Among those changes was burying the hatchet with Zwift, with whom Wahoo was in a year-long lawsuit, after Wahoo claimed the Zwift Hub smart trainer infringed on its patents. "If we work together, we can grow the industry," he said. "That was what Eric [Min, Zwift co-founder and CEO] and I set out to achieve."The ball had already begun rolling on this before Joyce’s appointment. The lawsuit was settled in September 2023, the Kickr Core Zwift One launched in March 2024, and Joyce was appointed in April. But he says working with Zwift - and other brands - is now central to how Wahoo should expand. An example of this includes Wahoo’s partnership with competitor brand Coros.Product plans and clearer prioritiesJoyce argued that Wahoo’s innovation and its ability to come up with good ideas can make it difficult to decide which to pursue."You tend to become a little chaotic with your product strategy because every idea is a good idea," he said. "When you try and make every product that you think is a good idea, you end up distributing your resources and a distributed focus."His solution to this was to revisit the company’s mission of "building the better athlete in all of us" and judge product ideas against it. Cycling remained – and still remains – the foundation, with indoor trainers, GPS computers and surrounding accessories supplying the data an athlete needs, but this is underpinned by software. The new Wahoo app was quietly rolled out this year, after a long period of beta testing. The revised strategy also meant an overhaul of its product launch cycles, which explains some of the recent quiet on the launch front."This year was a pretty lean year of releases for us, which was by design," Joyce explained. "Last year, when we kind of reset the product strategy, we then had to reset the engineering program."He expects the results to become more visible in 2027."Next year we have a pretty healthy set of product launches. I think we have seven or eight in the pipeline," he says. "I’m currently testing three of them as we speak. In fact, some of them are lying on my desk."Unfortunately he turned down my invite for a game of show and tell, despite me awkwardly presenting the Wahoo Elemnt Bolt 2 that was lying on my desk.Alongside that reset is a longer-term change to Wahoo’s product cycles and release cadence.I asked why the Kickr Core went from 2018 to 2025 without any update, while the flagship Kickr trainer grew to its sixth iteration – seven if you count the Kickr Move. "There was no rational reason for that replacement cadence," Joyce conceded. "The market was not demanding changes that quickly."Wahoo is now working around different cycles for different categories: roughly three years for bike computers, four for indoor trainers, and six for heart rate monitors and treadmills.I joked that he’s going to have a busy 2038 when those cycles overlap in their 12th year, to which he was keen to re-emphasise the use of the word "roughly" and affirmed that those are loose assumptions, rather than a fixed calendar. The slowed approach also reflects his view on indoor cycling, and the slowing nature of the technology’s innovation."I think it’s now entering that phase of iterative development rather than disruptive technology," he said. "That’s not to say it’ll never happen, but just right now, there’s not something that we see on the horizon of, let’s say, five years, that would be disruptive in nature."He immediately qualified that by adding "that doesn’t mean we’ve thought of everything." Wahoo didn’t cut its teeth in running, but in 2024, Wahoo launched a treadmill known as the Kickr Run. As Joyce explains, the plan was to take the formula that saw Wahoo transform indoor cycling, and apply it to another sport. It’s not quite had the same uptake in the 2.5 years since it launched as the smart trainer, but nevertheless Joyce sees it as an important growth category, and one where there’s plenty of opportunity for innovation and disruption. "Treadmills, for a very long time, have been terrible products," he says.And to that end, the Coros partnership adds weight to Wahoo’s move into running, but also demonstrates where Joyce believes Wahoo should avoid spreading itself thin. The Elemnt Rival smartwatch can’t hold a candle to the quality of launches from market leader Garmin, nor can Wahoo keep up with their annual release cycle. Instead, rather than invest in a complete watch range to compete directly, it chose to work with Coros."To develop multiple SKUs is a very big investment, takes a lot of time, and would distract our attention from the rest of the strategy," he explained.The goal is to provide access to products for cycling and running, indoors and outdoors, developing those products in house where possible, and partnering with others where not. Connecting indoor and outdoor trainingJoyce recognises that many of its customers aren’t exclusively doing one sport, nor are they only doing it indoors or out. "That boundary is no longer in and out of your house. It’s just cycling," he explained.And that’s where the Wahoo software offering comes into play. Wahoo has had multiple apps running concurrently for years, one controlling hardware and another providing training solutions, and Joyce is relieved at the recent consolidation. "If our mission is building the better athlete in all of us, and I can’t tell you whether you’re becoming a better athlete or not, then it’s kind of hard to make that brand play."If he can reduce the number of apps, or streamline the way in which the heart rate monitor, GPS computer and smart trainer all talk to third party suppliers, efficiencies can be found. Two approaches to artificial intelligenceWhen asked about AI, Joyce separated Wahoo’s use of the fast-growing tech into two buckets: internally, how the brand uses it day to day, and externally, i.e. what AI integration might offer customers. Within the business, AI is already used extensively across software, firmware and hardware engineering."We’ve seen significant acceleration in our development cycles of products, particularly software," he said, pointing to faster app updates as one example.He also said AI is being leveraged to help his Customer Service team resolve issues more quickly, while remaining entirely human. However, for consumer-facing features, such as the AI Coach revealed by Zwift this week, or the AI-based adaptive training used by TrainerRoad, Joyce is more cautious. He believes customers may prefer to use AI services they already pay for, whether that’s the aforementioned, or a direct account with Claude or Chat GPT.Voicing that customer’s perspective, he said: "I don’t want five licences for AI accounts. I want you to be able to pass me the data where I want it."That helps explain why Wahoo has yet to commit to a consumer AI offering, despite the fast pace of the industry. Where Joyce does see an opportunity, however, is in Wahoo’s enormous database of accumulated workout data. "We have records of workout data that goes back over a decade. We have the capability to translate that data into meaning, which is the next big opportunity we see, which we’re now starting to work on using machine learning and AI."And for that database of workout data, Joyce’s data is as prevalent as any others. "I love cycling. I love my running. To be able to go out on a Saturday and do a long ride and test stuff... yes, you could technically say that’s work, but for me it’s not."The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. Plus, the Cyclingnews app means you can stay up-to-date wherever you go!

item.title: Yankees news: Are Sato, Taira in play?
item.author: Nick Power
item.content:encoded: The Athletic | Chris Kirschner: ($) With the Yankees needing an upgrade at third base and the picking potentially slim, some have linked them to Teruaki Sato. The 27-year-old won the Triple Crown in Japan’s Central League last year and would provide a clear offensive upgrade. Kirschner throws cold water on the notion, noting that, like Munetaka Murakami, Sato’s defensive limitations could make him a better fit at first base. In a mailbag format, Kirschner also advocates for the Yankees cutting ties with Giancarlo Stanton and seeking competition for Spencer Jones in center.New York Post | Dan Martin: Another Japanese star, Kaima Taira, is set to be posted by the NPB’s Seibu Lions. The 5-foot-8 right-hander, who led his league with a 1.36 ERA as a starter last season, may project better as a reliever in the MLB. The Yankees have scouted Taira in the past and could make a play for his services. Any player looking to make the leap from Japan would need to factor in the impending lockout, which would necessitate their signing with a team by December 1st unless they are willing to wait until the labor dispute runs its course. (This happened to Seiya Suzuki during the last lockout.)MLPBA: The MLB Players Association announced the recipients of its Players Choice Awards Wednesday. Former Yankees pitching great David Cone received the Curt Flood Award, an honor which commemorates its namesake’s principled stand against the reserve clause which ended his playing career but helped bring about free agency. Cone, a longtime labor advocate who met Flood and served as American League player representative during the 1994-95 strike, called the award “the greatest honor of my baseball life.” Cam Schlittler was also honored with the AL Outstanding Pitcher, presaging his likely selection for the AL Cy Young.

item.title: How Herta compared to Perez in latest 2027 audition
item.author: Josh Suttill
item.content:encoded: Colton Herta might still somehow be one point short of a Formula 1 superlicence after a bizarre error, but his latest Cadillac F1 outing was an important audition to replace Valtteri Bottas next year.An incorrect calculation of his superlicence points (verified at the time by the FIA) means Herta erroneously thought completing 30 laps in his fifth FP1 outing of the season in Mexico would be enough to take him to the 40-point threshold required to finally earn him the superlicence he's been chasing for years."I was literally walking to go do the media stuff [after FP2], that was like the first time I had heard about it," Herta said on Friday evening. "Obviously, we were still doing our meetings and whatnot, so I haven't talked to anybody about it. As far as I was concerned, going into the weekend, if I did 100km here, I would have 40 [points]. "So, I'm not sure what's changed, or why stuff has changed, or if it even has. I have to wait and see. I think a lot of the people that I want to talk to about this are still in the meeting. Maybe I'll have a little bit more clarity this evening." Cadillac has gone beyond the mandated four rookie practice outings and given Herta a fifth session in Mexico to get him an extra point. It will run him again to get the final point, and had planned to anyway before the bizarre calculation error emerged. But his Mexico outing wasn't a case of Herta simply cruising around to get the mandated 100km of running to get the point. He was given an extensive programme that wasn't too dissimilar to the one conducted by Perez - his 2027 team-mate, should Herta secure Bottas's race seat. Herta's FP1 starts with an 11-lap stint on the hard tyres with a best lap of 1m22.452s, 1.067s slower than Perez's on the same tyres.Herta tells his engineer he's "leaving a lot on the table" in sector one, but he's told that's where he's actually faster than Perez; instead, he's leaking time in sectors two and three. This continues when he switches to the medium tyres, completing back-to-back stints on them with only a brief pitstop to go half a turn down on the front wing - a microadjustment to reduce the angle.It's on that second run when Herta completes his personal best lap, a 1m21.365s, on what are seven-lap-old tyres. Perez, by contrast, is able to complete his fastest lap on three-lap-old tyres during his first medium-tyre stint.The actual gap between them is 0.970s. Perez puts together his best three sectors; if you combine Herta's, he closes slightly to 0.817s. The Esses, in particular the Turn 10/11 right-left, are particularly challenging for Herta as he has to abandon one lap on the hard tyres when he cuts that corner, while another is wrecked by a wide moment there. He complained of "big understeer everywhere in the low-speed" corners. He struggled with his approach into the Turn 12 right-hander that leads into the stadium section; Herta's minimum speed drops to 13km/h below Perez's, so here alone he ships around four tenths to Perez on their fastest short runs. "The biggest thing was figuring out the timing for Turn 12," Herta said when The Race asked what his biggest limitation was. "The stadium section I think was all right. More so Turn 12. And then kind of sorted it out for the long run. "It's hard for the performance runs. You only do so many laps to sort it out in time. So unfortunately I didn't do that well. But for the long run it was better." Herta's claim stacks up as he generally halves that time loss in Turn 12 during his longer run at the end of the session.This is on average around eight tenths slower than Perez's, although it's hard to know the exact fuel loads of both cars. Herta called it the "most consistent part of my running", and the data backs that up with only a half-second variation in his laptimes over a seven-lap stint. A decent effort for a driver inexperienced in F1 machinery. Watching his FP1 onboard versus Perez, it was clear Herta needed more steering input around the lap and he was advised to better manage his throttle usage out of Turn 11 - corner exits being key to getting the most out of the 2026 power units. He's still adapting from his usual aggressive style that worked so well for him in IndyCar, "where without power steering you can be more aggressive"."You can have two or three or four inputs into the corner [in IndyCar], whereas in the Formula 1 car it's kind of useless effort," said Herta. "You have to be smooth and really precise with the line. Whereas in IndyCar you can maybe get away with a little bit more of a raggedy style."Really, that's just down to the lack of power steering in the IndyCar." F1 superlicence will be 'monkey off my back' Asked if he saw himself as a realistic contender for the 2027 Cadillac seat, Herta said: "I hope so. I don't know why I'd be doing this [otherwise]."I think Cadillac has shown a lot of faith in me in doing all these FP1s. They put a lot of resources behind me to get me ready to be in the F1 seat. "I hope that's all reciprocated, and I can make it." He added: "As far as 'now or never' - I don't think I can go back to IndyCar and have another chance in Formula 1. Whether that means next year or the following year. I really don't know what the plan is at the moment. "We'll have to wait and see. I think some decisions hopefully will be made within the next month. "It would be great the sooner the better to know going into November. You want to know what you're doing next year. For me, that's the main thing, is to know what I'm doing next year."Herta said "social media blows things up a lot more than in reality" so he's remaining calm amid rumours of him graduating to F1. But he did admit it will be a relief when he finally gets to the 40 superlicence points."Just maximising. Doing everything better. There's always time to find," Herta said when asked what he wants from his next FP1 outing."Just being able to maximise the short run and being able to maximise the long run. Probably a bit more in the short run than the long run. "But I think every time I get in the car I feel more comfortable and I'm able to push a bit more. "So I think once I kind of get that superlicence and that monkey off my back, then you can really kind of push everything as hard as you want to." The Race understands Cadillac was impressed with the job Herta did in Mexico, even if his ultimate pace was adrift of Perez's. It sees solid progression along Herta's F1 outings, and he remains a strong contender for a 2027 seat. At the same time, so do incumbent Bottas and the likes of Yuki Tsunoda and Mercedes reserve driver Fred Vesti. Vesti was particularly brash after FP1, where he was only 0.111s adrift of championship leader Kimi Antonelli in the sister Mercedes."I've got my eyes on that [Cadillac] seat," he said. "I believe I would be very, very good in that car, and to be in F1 has been my goal ever since I started driving. "I'm more motivated than ever; I'm extremely hungry to be on the grid." George Russell, who Vesti replaced for FP1, even said he told Mercedes: "I want to ensure that he [Vesti] gets an opportunity to show what he can do; that's the least that we could do." It was probably as strong an audition as Vesti could have hoped to make for the seat. And he wasn't the only rookie to set an eye-catching pace in FP1.Tsolov's impressive debutRed Bull junior Nikola Tsolov made the most of his F1 weekend debut to make his case for promotion to a race seat next year, lapping just 0.13s off Arvid Lindblad based on their headline laptimes on softs, and lapping two tenths quicker on mediums. To that we must add the caveat that there was evidence of differing energy strategies, with Lindblad often faster on the back straight and Tsolov stronger on the main straight - with Lindblad suffering one of the most extreme drop-offs in speed in the field prior to braking for Turn 1. Although Tsolov had a couple of laps deleted for track-limits violations, he was a little quicker than Lindblad in sector three, although he consistently lost time through and out of Turn 3. He was also perhaps a little conservative on the brakes into Turn 1 at the start of his best lap, perhaps not helped by the distraction of Isack Hadjar's Red Bull cruising off line approaching the corner. This was on the third push lap of his performance run on softs. Tsolov also had a problem with the seat impeding the bloodflow to his right leg. After setting his fastest lap, he reported that "I'm running out of blood in my right leg, I cannot feel my leg", and then suggested that "the seat is compressing my leg and my blood stopped". He returned to the garage and was able to return to the cockpit for another run after briefly standing up inside the car. "I've actually had that a few times before driving in F2," said Tsolov. "It's just the seat, I think, being a bit tighter than what we would like in my right leg. So my blood closed off. "When you press the full throttle, you move up into the seats, so you kind of compress your legs. That was the thing, I couldn't feel it. It was a dead leg, pretty much. You get the tingly feeling. And then it just came back, obviously. I had to shake it out and after two, three minutes, it came back."Slater's 'difficult' F1 debut Formula 3 runner-up Freddie Slater's F1 session debut was best summed up by the radio message he received, in which it was described as "a very difficult session from a technical point of view". That was an understatement, as he took the chequered flag after completing only 13 laps spread across six runs. Not that this was through any fault of the 18-year-old's. He started out with three single-lap runs. The first two of those focused on gathering aerodynamic data, with aero rakes mounted behind the front wheel and a nose change in between. He then should have been able to settle into a longer run on the hard Pirellis starting on his fifth lap, only to be told "we have to box this lap, we have an issue", entering Turn 7. This was because a fan had been left in the right-side sidepod cooling inlet, meaning Audi was fined €7500 for releasing the car in an unsafe condition. The team then sent Slater back out, but he was immediately called back in for a lengthy stay in the garage. He was able to return to the track with 11 minutes remaining, on a set of mediums. On his first push lap of the session, he posted a 1m22.451s, running deep in Turn 6 and compromising Turn 7. Then, on the second attempt, he locked up the front-left into Turn 1 and had to cut across the grass. The resulting flatspot meant he had to pit to switch back to hards, on which he had one push lap that stood at his fastest of the session - elevating him to 21st ahead of Herta. That put him 1.337s behind team-mate Nico Hulkenberg, which in the circumstances of his disrupted session and posting his best time on hards on only his second full flying lap was very respectable. "It's motorsport and that's how things go," said Slater of his stop-start running. "Of course, it was a bit frustrating obviously not to get many, many laps, but overall that one lap that I did do was actually pretty good compared to relevant data. And a really historic day for Audi to have their first junior driver in the car. "It's a very special day, so we look at the positives and then we focus on the results."

item.title: Relying on AI is rotting your brain. But here’s what you can do about it | Carly Dober
item.author: Carly Dober
item.content:encoded: Each new tech product is designed to make our lives easier and keep us mindlessly entertained. Switch off: embrace discomfort – and boredomEver longed for your own personal assistant? In the ever quickening tech race, Meta has recently launched Muse, a new AI personal agent. Unlike traditional chatbots, this little AI tool will be able to fill out forms for you, organise calendars, pay bills and make reservations. Meta describes Muse as a personal agent “built for everyone”. The launch comes at a time when AI agents have been making headlines for hacking into government websites, public agencies and businesses. However, my immediate concern is a little closer to home.I work as a psychologist, and I’m often talking to clients about lifestyle habits that lead to short-term gain but incur long-term pain. Our brains have a beautiful way of preferring the path of least resistance, of doing what is easiest to preserve our resources. And with the demands of modern life feeling so overwhelming for so many people, the urge to scroll after a long week or defer to a chatbot because you are exhausted is incredibly seducing.Carly Dober is a psychologist living and working in MelbourneContinue reading...

item.title: ‘The last fortress’: historic Athens cafe closes as countercultural area gentrifies
item.author: Helena Smith in Athens
item.content:encoded: Mouria coffeehouse unable to renew lease in Exarchia, known for leftwing solidarity, resistance and radicalismIt has been the hangout of writers, artists, poets and politicians, doctors and lawyers, radicals and revolutionaries for as long as anyone can remember. And for 44 years, Christos Vanas, the proprietor of Mouria, has let them all in.Every day at 7am, the taciturn former waiter has been the first man to step inside the historic cafe in Exarchia, the heart of leftwing Athens. It is a ritual he has kept punctiliously, opening up the famous gathering place before he himself has had his first coffee.Continue reading...

item.title: The Betting Coup That Rocked London’s Bookmakers Goes Unsolved
item.author: Sujata Rao
item.content:encoded: Lisa Lazarus, the top cop in US horse racing, woke up one morning this summer to find a flurry of missed overseas calls and e-mails. They were all from UK regulators and they all delivered the same urgent message: a series of large, unusual and suspiciously successful wagers on US races had been placed in London the day before, saddling some of the city’s famed betting parlors with hefty losses, and they needed her help.

item.title: Why politicians chasing economic growth is a lie | Radical Thinking with Aditya Chakrabortty
item.author: Presented by Aditya Chakrabortty with Karel Williams and Sukhdev Johal, produced by Frankie Tobi and Luke John Smith , the executive producers are Maz Ebtehaj, Kirsty Major and James Tindale
item.content:encoded: What if someone told you the truth about the economy? For years, UK governments have tried spending more, spending less, cutting red tape, leaving the EU, levelling up, and they have still failed to increase growth per person. So what’s the lesson from the great British fairytale? On the latest episode, the rebel economists Karel Williams and Sukhdev Johal explain to Aditya Chakrabortty why they believe praying for growth is a fool’s dream – and why it won’t improve your lifeAditya’s suggested reading list for Karel Williams and Sukhdev Johal:As we say in the podcast, I’ve championed the work of Karel and Sukhdev and their colleagues in the Guardian for many years, and some of my columns are a good introduction to their approach.• In our conversation we look at what life after growth looks like for towns and suburbs, and what it should look like. This report from South Wales in 2016 examines the present-day reality.• For a broader analysis of how the UK has become highly unequal and increasingly stagnant, try this.• As part of the Foundational Economy collective, Karel and Sukhdev put a lot of their analysis into freely available working papers. That circumvents the leisureliness and expense of academic publishing and gets their arguments in front of a wider public. item.title: Acosta wins chaotic Sepang MotoGP sprint
item.author: Eden Hannigan
item.content:encoded: Pedro Acosta claimed victory in a bizarre Sepang MotoGP sprint that was threatened by rain late on.Acosta came out on top of a four-way battle for the race win, prevailing by 0.578s over Marc Marquez, who increased his championship chances with second place. Marquez is now 19 points up on the absent Jorge Martin, and 52 points clear of Marco Bezzecchi.His brother Alex Marquez had got the start from pole position and led uncontested for four laps until he slid out of the race lead at Turn 14.The lead was then inherited by Ai Ogura, who had moved up to second place after an aggressive opening corner tussle with Marc.Spots of rain meant the white flag came out on lap two, allowing riders to swap bikes - with Jack Miller immediately prepared to take the gamble, but his Pramac Yamaha team not ready with his second bike, which frustrated him to no end.Iker Lecuona, Joan Mir and Franco Morbidelli were the first group to come in and successfully switch on lap five, but were setting times almost 10 seconds off the leaders’ pace, with Maverick Vinales the only other rider electing to change towards the end of the race. In the tricky conditions the top four bunched up, Ogura managing to hold off the challenges until Acosta attacked with three laps to spare.Although Ogura responded to the initial overtake from Acosta, he eventually ceded the position and slumped to fourth as his wet-weather demons made him no match for Marquez and Bezzecchi. He did, however, have a huge amount of breathing room to fifth-placed Fabio Di Giannantonio.Pecco Bagnaia overcame Brad Binder in their battle for sixth, while Diogo Moreira and Enea Bastianini picked up the final sprint points in eighth and ninth.1 Pedro Acosta (KTM) 2:00.357s2 Marc Marquez (Ducati) +0.578s3 Marco Bezzecchi (Aprilia) +1.310s4 Ai Ogura (Trackhouse Aprilia) +1.793s5 Fabio Di Giannantonio (VR46 Ducati) +5.053s6 Pecco Bagnaia (Ducati) +8.330s7 Brad Binder (KTM) +8.484s8 Diogo Moreira (LCR Honda) +9.001s9 Enea Bastianini (Tech3 KTM) +9.101s10 Johann Zarco (LCR Honda) +9.545s11 Fabio Quartararo (Yamaha) +10.076s12 Alex Rins (Yamaha) +12.250s13 Luca Marini (Honda) +12.715s14 Augusto Fernandez (Pramac Yamaha) +14.878s15 Maverick Vinales (Tech3 KTM) +1m42.843s16 Joan Mir (Honda) +1m43.826s17 Franco Morbidelli (VR46 Ducati) +1m45.065s18 Iker Lecuona (Gresini Ducati) +1m56.425sDNF Alex Marquez (Gresini Ducati)DNF Jack Miller (Pramac Yamaha)

item.title: Martin concedes 2026 MotoGP title is “already lost” after Malaysian GP withdrawal
Martin admits MotoGP title 'already lost' after Sepang withdrawal
item.author: Valentin Khorounzhiy
item.content:encoded: Aprilia MotoGP rider Jorge Martin feels the 2026 title is "already lost" following his withdrawal from the Malaysian Grand Prix weekend - but intends to ride in Qatar next week.Martin sustained a distal radius fracture in a crash during the Phillip Island sprint, but was back to riding just six days later at Sepang, in a desperate bid to keep himself in the championship picture and minimise the damage versus points leader Marc Marquez.But Martin was forced to give up on his weekend after three sessions, withdrawing after Saturday morning practice."I tried, I tried my best, I tried to ride, but for sure the process of healing is still early," he explained afterwards. "The healing is going really fast, but not enough to be efficient on the bike. I felt that I could ride with almost no pain, but for maybe one lap. After that I started to have a lot of pain, I couldn't be constant, so watching a bit the laptimes and my performance, we decided to stop, to try to wait. "We thought together with the team that the effort I was doing was too much to continue and yeah, nothing to gain. It was just going to be very difficult even to score one point."Martin said he just didn't have the requisite strength under braking - and made reference to his past efforts to shortcut recovery periods, particularly in an injury-laden 2025 and specifically in his return to racing in Qatar last year, in which he ran out of energy in the race, crashed and suffered a bad injury after being hit by a rival bike."It wasn't the best idea to continue," he said of this weekend, "because if I continue, it [shows] that I haven't learned anything from the past. "This happened to me in the past and I didn't want to crash or have a worse injury because of trying to race like this."Asked by The Race how he views the championship picture in light of his withdrawal, Martin admitted: "I think now I don't have to think about the championship. Maybe I can win it, but for me it's already lost. "So for sure I will fight till the end, not only for me, because at the end of the day I'm already a champion [in 2024], but for my team, for my people, I will fight till the end, I will try again in Qatar. Otherwise I would stay at home and rest."Martin trails Marquez by 10 points, with Marquez in position to triple or quadruple that lead at Sepang, having placed second in qualifying.Though Martin will return to Spain right away, as referenced above he still intends to try and race in Qatar next weekend, assuming that round goes ahead."During this week the improvement was incredible. I was able to ride a MotoGP with a broken wrist, so it's crazy. And I was under two minutes [in laptime]! So I'm already proud of my performance."My target is to go to Qatar. I will go there and I will try. Then if my feeling is the same, then I will have to stop. But this we will see in Qatar."

item.title: Martin out of Sepang MotoGP weekend, Alex Marquez on pole
item.author: Valentin Khorounzhiy
item.content:encoded: Alex Marquez took pole position for MotoGP's Malaysian Grand Prix and the sprint, as title hopeful Jorge Martin withdrew from the Sepang weekend.Martin, who fractured his wrist a week ago at Phillip Island, did three runs totalling eight laps in the 30-minute practice session before qualifying, and had to concede defeat in terms of continuing with the weekend."His feeling was better, to be honest, compared with yesterday, but he was not able to force in the braking," Aprilia team manager Paolo Bonora told MotoGP.com."The plan is to come back to Spain as soon as possible and to push on the recovery and to do his best to recover the situation. Coming back to Spain immediately, and then we check all together, during all the days, the situation, how it is improving, and we focus to have him in Qatar."With Martin now consigned to a non-score at Sepang, points leader Marc Marquez was close to maximising his qualifying, ultimately just 0.070s short of beating his brother.Alex Marquez had been the leader after the initial Q2 runs already, but was shuffled down to fifth by the end of the session - only to respond with a 1m56.493s that snatched pole from Marc.Pedro Acosta on the KTM will join the pair on the front row, having followed the elder Marquez very closely on both Q2 runs.Aprilia pair Ai Ogura and Marco Bezzecchi completed a top five covered by just 0.175s, with Fabio Di Giannantonio in sixth another 0.174s back from Bezzecchi.Q1 pace-setter Johann Zarco was limited to just one Q2 run but used Di Giannantonio as reference and so helped himself to eighth place, slotting in on row three between Enea Bastianini and Franco Morbidelli.Pecco Bagnaia, another Q1 graduate, ran 'off-sequence' in Q2 - doing his sole run mid-session, with no riders around him.After setting what proved to be his fastest lap he went off at Turn 1 and broke the windscreen in anger with his fist - though would have anyway been unlikely to improve.He placed 10th, ahead of Joan Mir and the injury-limited Maverick Vinales, who could not match his laptime from Friday.Honda riders Luca Marini and Diogo Moreira trailed stablemate Zarco by three and four tenths respectively in Q1, so were short of advancing into Q2 - while the rest of the field was never really in the mix.This included Gresini's Fermin Aldeguer stand-in Iker Lecuona, who has found Sepang the most difficult so far of the tracks he's ridden this season as a MotoGP replacement rider.1 Alex Marquez (Gresini Ducati) 1m56.493s2 Marc Marquez (Ducati) +0.070s3 Pedro Acosta (KTM) +0.084s4 Ai Ogura (Trackhouse Aprilia) +0.124s5 Marco Bezzecchi (Aprilia) +0.175s6 Fabio Di Giannantonio (VR46 Ducati) +0.349s7 Enea Bastianini (Tech3 KTM) +0.477s8 Johann Zarco (LCR Honda) +0.523s9 Franco Morbidelli (VR46 Ducati) +0.775s10 Pecco Bagnaia (Ducati) +0.794s11 Joan Mir (Honda) +0.850s12 Maverick Vinales (Tech3 KTM) +1.244s13 Luca Marini (Honda) +0.071s to Q214 Diogo Moreira (LCR Honda) +0.181s15 Brad Binder (KTM) +0.575s16 Jack Miller (Pramac Yamaha) +0.596s17 Alex Rins (Yamaha) +0.603s18 Fabio Quartararo (Yamaha) +0.667s19 Iker Lecuona (Gresini Ducati) +0.904s20 Augusto Fernandez (Pramac Yamaha) +1.303s

item.title: Ferrari is fastest in Mexico - but not for reasons rivals expected
item.author: Jon Noble
item.content:encoded: Ferrari’s rivals were right after all, but perhaps for the wrong reasons.The talk ahead of the Mexico Grand Prix had been that Ferrari’s smaller turbo design would give it a clear advantage at the high altitude track because it would in theory struggle less in the thinner air.So there was little surprise in the paddock when Charles Leclerc delivered a clean sweep of fastest laps in both FP1 and FP2 on Friday - confirming the Prancing Horse as the team to beat.What was perhaps more interesting from what we saw though - and which could play a big role in how the rest of the weekend plays out - was that Ferrari’s advantage was not coming from its turbo getting its boost pressure up quicker.Ferrari’s straight-line speed performance was notably lacking on the second and third straights. On its soft runs Leclerc was slowest of the top four teams into Turns 4 and 12.As Lewis Hamilton, who was sidelined by a suspected power unit problem halfway through FP2, remarked: “If you look at the speeds to the Mercedes and the Red Bull, they're still massive. "They're still quicker at the end of the straights, like they are in every race. So the turbo is just not making a difference. They are still pulling more at the end of the straights.“I think we're still losing a good two or three tenths. But the car is behaving really well fundamentally. Our car works really well, seemingly on a track like this.”Ferrari’s advantage in Mexico instead was coming from an area it has excelled in all season - low speed corner performance.It was just marginally better through the first two complexes of corners (Turns 1-3 plus Turns 4-6) as well as taking a decent chunk out of the opposition from Turn 12 into the stadium section.That trait meant that Leclerc had the consistency needed from the tyres to deliver the strongest long run of the afternoon - leaving rivals in no doubt about who was the benchmark.But while the opposition clearly was happy to put that favourite status on Ferrari, that does not necessarily mean that all hope is lost for everyone else.Others certainly saw enough in the data to think that there remains a big opportunity to fight at the front.When we look at the long run averages, Lando Norris in the McLaren, plus the Mercedes and Red Bulls were not far behind what Leclerc delivered once you factor in the influence of cool down laps and traffic.Mexican GP FP2 long run averagesRussell (soft): 1m21.442sAntonelli (medium): 1m21.487sLeclerc (medium): 1m21.163sPiastri (soft): 1m21.642sNorris (soft): 1m21.319sVerstappen (soft): 1m21.490sHadjar (soft): 1m21.369sIt was a day where certainly not everybody delivered to their maximum, as drivers battled brake locking, bumps and rapidly rising tyre temperatures.George Russell said: “Ferrari looked very strong and that was kind of the anticipation ahead of the weekend“I think we are still not fully on top of the new package, I think we see there's some balance limitations we have that we're struggling to overcome."I would say currently for Kimi and I, we're probably more outside the window, similar to what we saw in Malaysia, than inside the window like Kimi [Antonelli] achieved in Austin. Hopefully overnight we can get it back there."Things perhaps being a bit closer than they look at first glance is even more in play when you take into account that Verstappen’s afternoon was derailed by his clash with Liam Lawson that damaged his floor.That left the Dutchman battling a disconnected balance throughout his long run as he was lacking some key parts - so you could anticipate a potential improvement there.As Red Bull’s technical director Pierre Wache said: “Let's see tomorrow when the floor will be repaired and how the car is better or not.”Wache certainly felt that Ferrari was not out of reach, especially considering it has been strong in the types of turns that Mexico is full of.“I think in low-speed corners, since the beginning of the year, they are clearly on top of the game, and they have clearly a lot of downforce for low speed. After, let's see what we can extract. I think we are not far, and hope we can challenge them.” While the indications are of an early Ferrari advantage based on what we have seen so far, there are some important factors that mean it still cannot sleep easy tonight.The first element is that the long runs on Friday may not be totally representative of how things will play out in the race because of track temperature variations.The late start for FP2, allied to conditions being a bit cooler, meant that the track surface was not as hot as it will be on Sunday.Wache said it was not nailed on which would be the optimum tyre for the race.“The tyres are overheating in the last sector,” he said. “Clearly, the main problem is in FP2 where the track [temp] reduced by more than 10 degrees.“For the long run it was not very representative of what we'll see in the race Sunday. Then we have to be very careful on that aspect. So the deg will be higher, and maybe the medium will be better.”The premium on cooling around Mexico means that the pace of the cars is limited more by managing that than their theoretical best - so that could have a big impact too on how things play out on Sunday.Overtaking is already difficult here and following close behind a rival becomes far from ideal because of the consequences of engine and brake temperatures - so it is rarely a race where cars come through the field for the win. Clean air is invaluable.The need for Ferrari to not be in the pack is further increased by its expected turbo advantage having not manifested itself with superb top speed - something rivals were happy to see.As McLaren’s Oscar Piastri said: “I don’t think the turbo’s going to make as much of a difference as we thought.“They if anything looked a bit slow on the straights so, let’s wait and see tomorrow, definitely in some circumstances it will help them but I think in normal conditions it’s not as big of a factor as we first feared.” Put the 'track position is king' element on top of a likely one-stopper where there will not be strategy variation and it puts a huge premium on single-lap pace and delivering what is needed in Q3 to take pole position.And how many Fridays this season have ended with Ferrari topping the timesheets, looking to have the long-run potential, but then falling flat when things get serious on Saturday afternoon? We only need to go back one weekend for the last time that happened.Ferrari knows it has a weakness on Saturday based on it not being able to get its tyres as perfectly into the operating window as its rivals - and that could well prove critical in that fight at Mexico.As Hamilton remarked after practice: “I think the car feels like it's capable of competing in qualifying. But I don't know what it is they [the others] do in quali. Everyone seems to take a step. I don’t know if we can eke out a little bit more tomorrow.”At a track where the lack of downforce means tyres are sliding a lot more, everything may well come down to looking after those rears.Even Norris, who was second quickest in the afternoon, reckoned that the key would be delivering at the right moment.“The pace is definitely there but the field is incredibly tight at the minute, so it will come down to execution in tomorrow’s qualifying,” he said.Ferrari team boss Fred Vasseur knows that rivals have maybe not got things together as well as hoped on Friday and will come back stronger.So with things looking as tight as they are, amid what he says are “mega extreme” conditions, the fight for pole - which could be critical to the win - may well come down to simply who can keep their tyres alive the longest in qualifying.“It's always a challenge in Mexico,” said Vasseur. “I think it was last year that everybody was in half a tenth until Turn 10 and then you had four-tenths’ difference in two corners. I think it will be the same tomorrow.”

item.title: Stewards penalise Verstappen, Lawson after “unacceptable” F1 Mexico GP practice clash
Hadjar summoned for alleged paddock misconduct
item.author: Samarth Kanal
item.content:encoded: Isack Hadjar has been summoned by the stewards after alleged misconduct in the Formula 1 paddock at the Mexican Grand Prix. The FIA stewards called the Red Bull driver to see them for "misconduct relating to an incident in the Formula 1 paddock".The summons does not specify why Hadjar has been summoned.A video has circulated on social media appearing to show Hadjar pushing someone who tried to take a selfie with him. It is however unclear whether this is the reason Hadjar has been called to see the stewards at 10.15am local time on Saturday.As per the FIA's International Sporting Code, "any words, deeds or writings that have caused moral injury or loss to the FIA, its bodies, its members or its executive officers, and more generally on the interest of motorsport and on the values defended by the FIA" can carry a fine of up to €5000.Fines of up to €20,000 can be applied in other cases and the FIA's sporting code says: "For very serious offences, more severe penalties under the ISC [international sporting code] may be imposed."Aggravating or mitigating circumstances can however change the penalty imposed.

item.title: Verstappen and Lawson get grid drops for 'clumsy' Mexico clash
item.author: Jack Cozens
item.content:encoded: Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson have each been given one-place grid penalties for their "clumsy" clash during second Formula 1 practice at the Mexican Grand Prix.That incident occurred early in FP2 when Verstappen, on a prep lap, tried to lunge past Lawson - on a cooldown lap before another push - into the 90-degree Turn 12 right-hander.Lawson stayed on the outside of Verstappen through that corner, which became the inside line for the Turn 13 switchback in the stadium section, before Verstappen cut across the track at Turn 14 and got ahead of the Racing Bulls driver, though only via contact that shattered the Red Bull's left-side bargeboard, with the resulting debris prompting a red flag.Verstappen told Sky Sports F1 it was "not very smart behaviour" from Lawson, who (alongside team-mate Arvid Lindblad) has not yet been announced at Racing Bulls for 2027 and whom Verstappen characterised as "fighting for your seat".Verstappen said of the incident: "At the end of the day, it's not going to change my weekend."But the clash did have consequences.In identical statements issued to both cars, the stewards said they considered both drivers' actions "unacceptable", in particular in respect of a "warning" given at the team managers' meeting earlier on Friday.They said both Lawson and Verstappen had called the move "clumsy" and unnecessary - a word also used by Racing Bulls team principal Alan Permane when describing the contact.It was that message given at the team managers' meeting that ultimately condemned Verstappen and Lawson to penalties."Noting that there had been similar incidents this year of actions between drivers in free practice, the stewards have decided to escalate the penalty from that of a formal warning to a grid position penalty particularly in view of the warning that had been provided at the team managers' meeting and consistent with other incidents involving contact between the cars in free practice in previous years," the stewards' decision read.Both drivers were also given one penalty point for the transgression.

item.title: 76ers 98, Knicks 93: “Unfortunately it took us too long to show up tonight.”
item.author: Russell Richardson
item.content:encoded: Last season, en route to a World Championship, the New York Knicks (2-4) took a pleasant detour in Las Vegas to collect the Emirates NBA Cup. The road to repeating the Cup win is rocky this season, with their Group B considered to be the toughest.Tonight, they traveled to Pennsylvania to face the 76ers at the Xfinity Mobile Arena on a garish blue and gold cartoon court. This was their first Cup game of the season and the 482nd meeting between the two franchises. The Philadelphia 76ers (5-1) came in tied with Detroit for first place in the East. All night, the star-heavy squad showed the secret to their success so far this season—a stingy, sticky defense that limited New York to 32% perimeter shooting. Our heroes fell behind by double digits toward the end of the first quarter and stayed behind until the final two minutes of the game. Quoth Laurenpal, “Unfortunately it took us too long to show up tonight.” Despite a clutch bucket from Jalen Brunson (24 PTS, 8-22 FG) for the lead late in the fourth, Tyrese Maxey (27 PTS, 10-19 FG) and the Sixers were too strong to keep down. Your final: 98-93.Through the first half of the first quarter, the home team had the edge, with Maxey, Joel Embiid (10 PTS, 7 RBS, 7 AST), LeBron James (20 PTS, 9 RBS, 8 AST), and VJ Edgecombe (13 PTS, 8 RBS) combining for 14 points. Across the floor, Karl-Anthony Towns (22 PTS, 12 RBS), OG Anunoby (9 PTS, 4-10 FG), Mikal Bridges (12 PTS, 3 STL, 5-8 FG), and Brunson had posted 11 for the visitors.Part of the problem for our heroes was that Philly played an almost mistake-free opening frame, committing one foul and zero turnovers. And their defensive intensity—they’re top-five in the league—complicated every Knicks shot. When Tyler Kolek (2 PTS, 4 AST, 13 MIN) subbed in with about three minutes left, he was harassed into his first TO of the season. Further proof of that good D? The good guys shot just 27% in the first period.On one sequence, Brunson dribbled against Maxey from 18 feet, left side, one-on-one. Maxey blocked him, but Cap retained the ball and swished a jumper on his second attempt. It was a rare instance of Maxey getting outplayed. He led all first-half scorers with 15 points. Brunson managed only seven points pre-intermission.After a Philly timeout, Mike Brown sent in Landry Shamet (0 PTS, 0-3 FG, 16 MIN), Miles McBride (10 PTS, 4-8 FG, 24 MIN), and Andre Drummond (3 PTS, 6 RBS, 12 MIN). The guests missed five shots, during which time the hosts capitalized with interior scores. After surrendering eight unanswered points, the Knicks got relief when Josh Hart (7 PTS, 6 RBS, 31 MIN) delivered from deep. By the quarter break, the home team was up 29-21.On to the second. Philly moved the ball well and was unafraid to drive the lane, as Maxey did with an emphatic throwdown. While Brunson rested—and Jose Alvarado sat out with a sprained ankle—Kolek continued to play. He gave up a second turnover. Cap checked back in around the seven-minute mark.At the midway point, LeBron and Hart traded bombs from the perimeter. The differential reached 14 before the Knicks began to chisel it down.McBride made some midrange shots from the elbow. It was nice to see a little more imagination in his usage, rather than just sticking him at the arc and waiting for a pass. He also grabbed a timely offensive board in the paint among Embiid and a couple of other big bodies.Nevertheless, the Knicks couldn’t get a run going. A corner three by Bridges cut the gap to six, but Maxey chucked from deep for three of his own. In fitting fashion, Brunson couldn’t get open for a final shot, and the halftime buzzer buzzed without an attempt. Philly up, 53-44.The Knicks had out-rebounded Philly (23-19) and shot slightly better from deep (32% to 29%), but Philly owned everything inside the arc. The Knicks took more than half their shots from deep and scored nothing on fast breaks, which is a tough way to keep pace while conceding so much inside. No Knick had reached double digits yet; KAT led the team with nine points.Following intermission, Hart missed from deep, Bridges threw the ball to the front row, and Maxey scored five points. Philly went up by 14, matching its biggest advantage yet.Finding the previous events intolerable, Brunson took the reins and commanded his squad on an 11-1 run. He scored seven straight during that burst, and Bridges redeemed his TO with a steal (ripping the ball out of Edgecombe’s mitts) and a longball. After that, Nurse needed a timeout for a breather and a regroup.Whatever advice the coach imparted, it worked. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Anfernee Simons (21 PTS, 5-8 3PT, 31 MIN) hit triples, Philly tightened its defense, and LeBron attacked the cup. Soon enough, the Knicks trailed by ten again and gave us great concern about their ability to rally for a lead. After a Mike Brown timeout, two consecutive Shamet turnovers and another Simons jumper further pushed the score in the wrong direction. Too many one-and-dones were a problem. The Knicks wouldn’t quit and swung back, with McBride and Brunson reducing the hole to six, but a Simons bomb with five seconds to go closed the quarter at 77-68.Jordan Clarkson, a sparkplug in Chicago, made his first appearance to start the final frame. Alongside him: Kolek, McBride, Anunoby, and Towns. They manufactured buckets, but surrendered them, too. Simons continued to rain buckets.One of the surprising strengths of Clarkson’s game has been his offensive rebounding. When he flew through traffic to tip in a missed McBride three, it wasn’t quite a Game Four highlight, but it sliced the differential to three. That was the closest the team had been since midway through the first. But they taketh, they giveth. Embiid drilled a jumper at the other end, and with six-ish minutes left, Mike Brown needed a timeout.Out of the timeout, Brown’s lineup was Brunson, Clarkson, Bridges, Hart, and Towns. The choice to go with Clarkson’s offense over Anunoby’s defense was a curious gamble. Both teams were careening up and down the court at top speed, even that geezer LeBron, and when KAT rifled a bomb, a mere two points separated the two teams.In crunch time, Brunson had a look but bricked from deep. The ball came back to him, but LeBron worked him into a jam, with Jalen having to throw the ball off him out of bounds. After the inbound, Jalen had another chance—and connected from deep for their first lead since the opening minutes!LeBron answered with a fadeaway at 1:10 to reclaim the lead. After Cap missed a floater, Edgecombe knocked down his first triple of the night. 94-90, 34 seconds remaining.Cap got the ball again, iso-ing on Edgecombe, but slipped and turned his right ankle in a legitimately terrifying moment. Edgecombe was called for a ticky-tack foul (foot-to-foot contact). Brunson made one freebie. 94-91, 31 seconds. At the other end, Maxey hustled through traffic and missed on a contested layup, but ’Bron swept in for the putback. That put the score at 96-91 with 12 seconds on the clock. New York needed a miracle, but the gods were fresh out. Anunoby made a dunk, and Philly added two free throws. Ball game.Back to work on Monday, at home against the Nets. Safe travels, Knickerbockers.

item.title: Once again, NASA is asking for ideas to rescue Hubble from certain death
item.author: Stephen Clark
item.content:encoded: The Hubble Space Telescope still shines in the eyes of astronomers after 36 years in orbit, but it is not as nimble as it once was. Left alone, the observatory will plunge back into the atmosphere in the early-to-mid-2030s, closing the book on one of the most famous scientific instruments of the century.NASA last raised the orbit of Hubble in 2002, when the Space Shuttle visited the observatory for a servicing mission. The final shuttle servicing flight in 2009 did not reboost the telescope's orbit, and with the retirement of the shuttle fleet two years later, Hubble has steadily lost altitude with no way to stave off eventual destruction.The space agency released a Request For Information (RFI) on Thursday asking commercial companies for ideas on how to reboost, service, or a controlled disposal of Hubble. Responses are due November 30. Specifically, NASA is looking for information about companies' current and near-term capabilities for capturing Hubble and boosting it to an altitude of at least 373 miles (600 km), enhancing the telescope's performance, or guiding Hubble to a controlled reentry.

To date, 74 animal cases have been identified in the US since the flies re-invaded the country in June.The flies lay hundreds of eggs in wounds and moist orifices of animals, and the resulting voracious maggots feast on their victims. The maggots resemble screws and tortuously bore and twist into living flesh, causing severe, sometimes fatal wounds, before dropping to the ground to develop into adults.

item.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
item.author: Dan Goodin
item.content:encoded: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident.The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont. Both Beaumont and the CTO and co-founder of security firm Phorian said that version 2.1.313 was distributed through Anthropic’s official account on Cursor. So far, neither Cursor nor Anthropic has explained how the attackers gained control of the account.In search of cloud credentials“It was a supply-chain compromise where the attacker gained access to the official distribution channel,” Phorian CTO and co-founder Luke Roberts told Ars. “The malicious version 2.1.313 was posted to the official Anthropic account, effectively superseding 2.1.312. Extensions auto-update in Cursor by default, but users can configure this in settings.” Phorian has more details here.

item.title: Over 25% of people lie to get antibiotics—and their lies aren't even good
item.author: Beth Mole
item.content:encoded: A significant number of patients in the US lie to their doctors to get antibiotics they likely don't need, according to two new studies. While that may not be a startling revelation, the studies drills down on the phenomenon, finding that the lies patients tell are generally bad ones—and yet, they work almost all the time.In the two linked studies published Friday in JAMA Network Open, a team of researchers led by Alistair Thorpe at the University of Utah analyzed online survey data from over 1,000 adults. They found that over a quarter of people reported having lied to a clinician at least once to get an antibiotic prescription for themselves or a child in their care. Patients lied by either exaggerating symptoms, making up symptoms, or—most often—both.But interestingly, the lies people told to get antibiotics involved making up or exaggerating symptoms of infections that wouldn't be treated with antibiotics. For example, the most common falsehoods were symptoms associated with colds, such as fever, cough, and sore throat. That's despite the fact that colds are caused by viruses, not bacteria—which antibiotics treat.

item.title: 'A contract is about more than salary' - The Cyclists' Alliance 2026 rider survey finds financial insecurity, health and safety issues among the main concerns of the women's peloton
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: The Cyclists' Alliance, a leading labour organisation in women's cycling, has released the findings of its 2026 rider survey. Financial insecurity beyond the Women's WorldTour level and health, welfare and safety issues are the top concerns among 127 riders (118 road riders) surveyed.The 'State of the Professional Women's Peloton 2026' report found that the sport is currently "creating opportunities" while still leaving riders lacking "the financial security, care and development pathway they need."The six priorities for women's cycling based on the responses gathered, according to the TCA, include financial security, race safety, health and welfare, safeguarding, development, and broadcast visibility.The financial aspect of the report found that 75% of the 52 Continental racers who responded to the survey receive no salary from their team, while 52% reported uncovered travel costs. Of riders at Continental level, 73% cited financial pressure as the main factor in considering quitting the sport.In response, The Cyclists' Alliance has asked the UCI to revise and strengthen its model contract to ensure riders' "essential racing costs" are covered, as well as verifying teams can meet their commitments."A contract is about more than salary. Riders need to know what protection they have, and where the gaps are; if they face injury, pregnancy, illness or a change in their team’s plans. TCA members can access independent contract and legal advice before signing and when problems arise," said TCA legal and ethics officer, Judith van Maanen.On the issue of rider safety, over 60% of respondents cited road furniture, rider behaviour, poor road surfaces, and unsafe final kilometres as concerns.Only 17% of Continental respondents have access to regular medical screening, compared with 90% of riders in the Women's WorldTour, while 23% of respondents reported negative or toxic team environments as a factor in considering quitting the sport.The Cyclists' Alliance has requested that the UCI establish RED-S screening in mandatory medical monitoring, safeguards for riders recovering from injury, more "female-specific research" into the health demands of the women's peloton, that riders be able to access "confidential, independent support", and that more stringent verification of staff qualifications and safeguarding credentials be put in place."You don’t have to wait until something becomes misconduct to ask for help. If a comment, request or relationship makes you uncomfortable, or simply doesn’t feel right, talk to us to understand the situation, your boundaries and your options. You will be listened to," said Van Maanen.Elsewhere, development pathways for young riders were raised as an issue, with the cancellation of the 2026 Tour de l'Avenir Femes and the switch of several races from 1.2 to 1.1 highlighted as examples of roads to the top of the sport being closed.Full coverage of the biggest races on the calendar, such as the Tour de France Femmes and Paris-Roubaix Femmes, was also raised by 49% of respondents, with greater coverage leading to bigger audiences, higher sponsor value, and more investment in the sport.The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down.
